ai.description: This snake reaches 60 cm. It has a blunt head, large eyes, and a brown body with dark crossbands. Distinctive features include a vertically compressed body and specialized jaw for eating slugs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Pareas monticola* is best distinguished by its single prefrontal scale, which separates the internasals from the frontal, unlike the two prefrontals found in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Pareas monticola* inhabits dense, humid subtropical and temperate forests in the Himalayas and Northeast India, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Montane Slug-eating snake is primarily nocturnal and possesses specialized asymmetrical jaws that allow it to efficiently extract snails from their shells.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pareas monticola* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatching observed between August and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Pareas monticola* is found in the Eastern Himalayas and Northeast India, primarily inhabiting forested regions at elevations between 500 and 2,000 meters.
